blogs.title: How to Choose the Right TV Wall Mount for Your Screen
blogs.author: Admin
blogs.excerpt: Fixed, tilting, or full-motion? Here's how to pick the perfect mount for your TV size and wall type.
blogs.content:
Choosing the right TV wall mount starts with your screen size, wall type, and how flexible you want the viewing angle to be.

Fixed mounts work well when you want a clean, flush installation. Tilting mounts help reduce glare in bedrooms and higher wall positions. Full-motion mounts are ideal when you need to swivel, extend, or change viewing angles between seating areas.

Before installation, always confirm the VESA pattern, wall strength, and cable route. A strong mount paired with proper installation keeps the screen secure and the final finish neat.

blogs.title: Top 5 Benefits of Solar Outdoor Lighting in Kenya
blogs.author: Admin
blogs.excerpt: Solar lights cut your electricity bill, improve compound security, and require zero wiring. Here's why they're worth it.
blogs.content:
Solar outdoor lighting is one of the easiest ways to improve visibility, security, and convenience around your property.

It reduces electricity costs, works in areas where wiring is difficult, and helps light up gates, pathways, compounds, and parking areas. Modern solar fittings also charge efficiently and provide dependable nighttime lighting.

When selecting solar lights, consider brightness, battery capacity, panel size, and weather resistance. The right setup gives you reliable lighting with very low maintenance.

blogs.title: CCTV Camera Placement: Where to Install for Maximum Coverage
blogs.author: Admin
blogs.excerpt: Proper camera placement makes the difference between effective surveillance and blind spots. Here's a practical guide.
blogs.content:
Effective CCTV coverage depends more on camera placement than camera quantity.

Entrance points, perimeter walls, parking areas, cashier points, and corridors are usually the highest-priority positions. Cameras should be mounted high enough to avoid tampering while still keeping faces and motion clearly visible.

Avoid pointing cameras directly into strong light sources and always test night performance before finalizing the setup. A well-planned layout reduces blind spots and improves recorded evidence quality.
